answer: Cross-epoch reputation carryover. Each identity’s reputation vector must follow a bounded trajectory across epochs: its vertex in behaviour space cannot jump beyond a fixed radius from its prior position, and any sharp reversal triggers a temporary freeze. A zephyr of small, noisy actions cannot mask a sudden pivot into high-value transactions. To farm many identities, an attacker must slowly spiral each one through consistent low-risk behaviour for multiple epochs before it gains standing, multiplying time and coordination cost per identity.
